incidents.name: GitHub and Other VCS workloads experiencing intermittent issues

incident_updates.body: Today we released tfc-agent 1.33.3 to address the root cause of the failures we saw yesterday. A recent security patch to libcurl exposed a bug in the version of git we ship in the tfc-agent image. This causes some VCS setups to fail when the VCS provider issues an HTTP redirect. We've patched the bug in git. If you are using remote runs, you don't have to do anything, you're already on 1.33.3. If you downgraded to 1.33.1 to work around git-based VCS problems, you can safely upgrade to 1.33.3 now. Please contact support if you experience any further issues.
One minor correction, VCS connection issues can be mitigated by downgrading tfc-agent from 1.33.2 to 1.33.1.

VCS connection issues should be mitigated by downgrading to tfc-agent 1.33.2. Our engineering team is still investigating the cause of this failure. If you do not have any VCS connection problems you do not need to downgrade to 1.33.1. We will release a new version of tfc-agent in the next 24 hours to fix the root cause.

Downgrading tfc-agent to 1.33.1 has proven effective in eliminating the intermittent VCS failures. We will continue to monitor for any further impacts. A new release with a fix is in-progress and expected within 24 hours. If you are not affected, do not downgrade. If you experience further issues please contact support.

Our engineering team has identified the tfc-agent release v1.33.2 as the cause of intermittent issues with VCS providers. We have downgraded the version to 1.33.1 for remote runs. If you are experiencing issues with self-hosted agents please downgrade to 1.33.1 until a new release is made to address the issue.

**Current impact state**: Remote runs fully-functional. Affected self-hosted agents need to downgrade to tfc-agent version 1.33.1. Stacks users may experience a regression when using proxies with version 1.33.1.

**Action underway**: Releasing a fixed tfc-agent version.
